# Temple Scroll Column 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 11 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 11:2 — "laborious work" vs. "heavy labor" — register of prohibition

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all laborious work you shall not do" | Hebrew word order preserved; melekhet avodah rendered literally |
| LOGOS | "You shall do no laborious work" | Standard English word order; "laborious work" retains technical legal sense |
| PNEUMA | "You must not do any heavy labor" | "Heavy labor" more natural in modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Laborious work" preserves the technical cultic term while maintaining standard English syntax. EMET's inverted word order is unnecessarily opaque; PNEUMA's "heavy labor" loses the connection to the specific Hebrew legal category melekhet avodah.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:5 — "bring near" vs. "present" vs. "bring" — sacrificial verb hiqriv

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall bring near a burnt offering" | Literal rendering of hiqriv preserving the spatial/cultic sense |
| LOGOS | "you shall present a burnt offering" | "Present" captures the formal offering sense |
| PNEUMA | "You are to bring a burnt offering" | Simple, natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "offer" as a compromise — the standard English sacrificial verb that is both accurate and natural. EMET's "bring near" is too literal for English idiom; PNEUMA's "bring" is too casual for cultic legislation.

**Status:** Resolved with compromise. "Offer" used in consensus text.

---

## 11:7 — "sons of a year" vs. "yearling" vs. "one-year-old"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "lambs, sons of a year" | Literal rendering of bene shanah |
| LOGOS | "yearling lambs" | Standard biblical translation convention |
| PNEUMA | "one-year-old lambs" | Most transparent to modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "yearling lambs" (LOGOS). This is the standard rendering across major English Bible translations and is immediately understood. EMET's literalism is a Hebraism unfamiliar in English; PNEUMA's version is clear but slightly verbose.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:8 — grain offering measurement unit — explicit vs. implicit

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "three-tenths for the bull" | Omits unit; assumes reader knows the ephah measure |
| LOGOS | "three-tenths of an ephah for the bull" | Supplies the unit for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "three-tenths of a measure for the bull" | Generic "measure" for accessibility |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The ephah is the specific unit prescribed in the Pentateuchal parallel (Num 29:3) and should be named. PNEUMA's vague "measure" sacrifices precision; EMET's omission assumes too much background knowledge.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 11:15 — "statute forever" vs. "perpetual statute" vs. "lasting requirement"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a statute forever throughout your generations" | Literal chuqqat olam ledoroteikhem |
| LOGOS | "a perpetual statute throughout your generations" | "Perpetual statute" is standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "a lasting requirement for all your generations" | "Requirement" more accessible than "statute" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Perpetual statute" is the established rendering for chuqqat olam in biblical translation. PNEUMA's "requirement" dilutes the legal-cultic gravity of the term. EMET's "statute forever" is acceptable but less idiomatic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
